D22·t4b1 — 2026-09-16 — replaced by D47·f4yz
rule: Platform packages are named `sofar-core-<platform>-<arch>`, generated only by packaging/npm/emit.mjs, versioned in lockstep with sofar.sh, and published before sofar.sh; hook shims carry routing to `sofar-core` and nothing else.
chose: The native core ships as unscoped npm platform packages `sofar-core-<platform>-<arch>` (darwin arm64/x64, linux x64/arm64, win32 x64), each holding the binary and nothing else — no bin, no scripts — generated by packaging/npm/emit.mjs (the single source of the platform list, the names and the version lockstep; `--check` in CI and the packaging test) and declared as optionalDependencies of sofar.sh at sofar.sh's exact version; boot.ts's CORE_PACKAGE (now cli/core.ts, shared with `sofar doctor`'s new "hot path:" finding) resolves that name, replacing D31's provisional `@sofar/core-*`. The binary reaches PATH through sofar.sh itself: `bin/sofar-core` is a JavaScript shim equal to `sofar` that postinstall (install.mjs) replaces with the platform package's binary on non-Windows, silently leaving the shim when there is no package or scripts are off. The hook shims route before they exec — `sofar-core event <hook>` when `command -v` finds one (SOFAR_CORE=0 forces the CLI, SOFAR_CORE=<path> names a core), else `sofar event <hook>` — so a hook on the core is one exec of native code with no node in front. CI gains a five-runner `core` matrix (fmt, clippy -D warnings, test, release build, artifact upload) and a `core-conformance` job running the unfiltered mixed-install suite, fold-parity, render-parity, `cargo xtask schema --check` and `emit.mjs --check`; publishing (platform packages first, then sofar.sh) stays the human step per repo memory M1. Verified: npm 11 resolves and installs sofar.sh with the five packages unpublished (lockfile records them `optional: true`, install succeeds, the shim answers); the packaging test installs the locally staged platform package next to sofar.sh in a temp prefix and proves the postinstall replacement byte-identical, `sofar-core status` by PATH name, the init-installed shim exec'ing it, and `sofar status` through the stub and with SOFAR_CORE=0 rendering the same bytes.
over: The `@sofar/…` scope (the npm token in this environment is invalid, E401, so scope ownership could not be checked; the only published package is unscoped sofar.sh); a `bin` entry on each platform package (npm links only the top-level package's bins on a global install, so it would not reach PATH); symlinking instead of copying in postinstall (a pruned or swapped platform package would leave a dead link on PATH — worse than the shim); a postinstall download of the binary (network at install time, and BD1's "the tarball is the product boundary"); baking a machine path into the committed .claude/hooks shims (shared by every clone); running CI publishes with an NPM_TOKEN (M1: the user publishes, OTP).
because: esbuild's layout (optional platform packages + a postinstall that swaps a shim for the binary) is the proven shape for exactly this problem and degrades to "no core" on every failure path, which is the 3.1 fallback world already proved byte-identical; unscoped names are publishable by the existing sofar.sh owner without an org; routing in the shim is not behaviour (BD4 — the CLI still owns every byte) and is the only way a hook avoids node's boot, which HOTPATH measured at ~32 ms of every hook and which D5 says only `npm run perf` may quantify.
